newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-GIANTS NAME FASSEL NEW HEAD COACH.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-GIANTS NAME FASSEL NEW HEAD COACH.

text.p: The New York Giants, aiming to revitalise their offence and quarterback Dave Brown, hired Arizona Cardinals assistant Jim Fassel on Wednesday as their new head coach.
The 47-year-old Fassel, who served as quarterbacks coach for the Giants in 1991 and 1992, succeeds Dan Reeves, fired at the end of New York's 6-10 season.
"I feel confident we have the right coach for the right sport for the right town," Giants general manager George Young said.
Terms were not disclosed but reports indicated Fassel would receive more than $3 million over the four-year deal.

Fassel has a reputation for bringing out the best in quarterbacks, a talent which will be put to a supreme test with Brown and the Giants, whose offence ranked dead last in the NFL in both passing and total offence.

"Dave needs to be in a situation where he is sure of himself and has confidence," Fassel said. "I think Dave Brown is an excellent quarterback and can be a lot better than he is. It's my job to make him play better."
Fassel says he will call all the offensive plays and that Brown will enter training camp as the number one quarterback over backup Danny Kanell.
"I want to head off a quarterback controversy," he said.
Fassel has received praise for his coaching techniques from quarterbacks John Elway, Phil Simms, Jeff Hostetler and Boomer Esiason, all of whom have played in the Super Bowl.
The Giants were 5-11 in 1995 and have failed to make the playoffs the last three seasons and five of the last six.

After leaving the Giants in his first stint on the staff, Fassel served as offensive coordinator with Denver in 1993-94 and quarterbacks coach for the Oakland Raiders in 1995 before becoming offensive coordinator for the Cardinals.
Fassel's only head coaching stint was at the University of Utah from 1985 to 1989. His top player at Utah was current Detroit Lions quarterback Scott Mitchell.

The personable Fassel is expected to be a better fit than Reeves, who was often uncomfortable with the team's hierarchy in which Young gives a great deal of power to player personnel director Tom Boisture.
"I sat in that draft room. I know what went on," said Fassel, who is confident he will have input in the Giants' structure.
One of Fassel's most important tasks will be the hiring of a defensive coordinator. Mike Nolan, who held the job under Reeves last season, left for the same job with the Washington Redskins.
